headline: Bank Indonesia Raises Benchmark Interest Rate to 6.00% to Support Rupiah
summary: Bank Indonesia raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.00%. Governor Destry Damayanti said the tightening is aimed at stabilizing the domestic currency and containing inflation.
why: Bank Indonesia is the central bank of Southeast Asia's largest economy, managing monetary policy and foreign exchange stability.

impacts.name: Indonesian Rupiah
impacts.why: Higher policy interest rates bolster capital inflows and support domestic currency valuation.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The unexpected rate hike directly tightened monetary conditions to defend the domestic exchange rate.
